summary: A variant of normal React state that also saves its value in the browser's local storage so it survives page reloads.
purpose: Remembers chart and tool settings for each tool or industry when no saved deck exists.
why: The comment says chart settings should survive reloads. Bad saved data is rejected so the app falls back to safe defaults.
how: On start, it reads the saved value under the given key, checks it with the validator, and uses it only if valid. Every time the value changes, it writes the new value back. If the key changes, it reloads the value for the new key.
inputs: A storage key, a starting value, and a validator function that confirms a value has the right shape.
outputs: The current value and a setter, used the same way as normal React state.
risks: Corrupted or outdated saved values are ignored. Storage can be full or blocked, in which case changes are silently not saved.
debug: Open the browser's developer tools and inspect local storage for the key. Delete the key to reset the setting. If a setting never saves, check whether storage is blocked in private browsing.
